_comment: The published price of credit. This file is the single source: domain.js, the application form and the prose on the site are all checked against it by scripts/check-rates.mjs, so a change here is a change everywhere or CI fails. Served publicly on purpose — these rates are published.

terms._comment: Weeks to flat interest percent, applied once to the principal and never compounded.

overdue._comment: Applies when a loan passes its final due date. The penalty REPLACES the term rate rather than adding to it: a 4-week loan at 30% becomes 35% in total, not 65%. It is a single flat rate, not a ladder — stepPercent 0 holds it at startPercent however long the loan runs.
overdue._flatComment: Decided 3 November 2026: the delay penalty is a flat 35%, whatever the length of the delay. Someone two days late and someone six months late owe the same — K5,400 on K4,000 borrowed for four weeks. The engine still supports a ladder; setting stepPercent above 0 turns it back on and every band, cap and next-step date below starts working again, with no code change.
overdue._capComment: Interest would stop at the principal, so the most anyone could owe is twice what they borrowed — the in duplum rule applied across the region. Dormant while stepPercent is 0, since a flat 35% never approaches it. Kept so the protection is already in place if the ladder is ever switched back on. Confirm against whatever cap the Bank of Zambia sets under the Banking and Financial Services Act No. 9 of 2026 before relying on it.
overdue._eightWeekGap: A flat 35% penalty sits below the 45% charged for the 8-week term, so an overdue 8-week loan is held at its term rate by the floor in av_amount_owing() and carries NO late charge at all, however long it runs. Raised with the owner on 3 November and accepted. The fix, if it is ever wanted, is a per-term penalty rather than one flat figure — never removing the floor, which is what stops an overdue loan costing less than an on-time one.
overdue._fourWeekGap: A 4-week loan that defaults costs K5,400, against K5,800 for borrowing 8 weeks honestly, so defaulting is K400 cheaper at any point past week four. Raising startPercent to 46 or above would close it. Left as specified; asserted in tests/rates.test.mjs.

legacy._comment: Loans signed before this file existed carry their own late terms in the record's late_payment_rate field, written at signing (7.5% per week overdue, additive, entered by staff). Those agreements are binding as signed. The engine never applies the ladder above to them.
